cases.title: Motor collision, rear-ended at a signal
cases.description: Rear-ended by a truck while stopped at a traffic signal. Rear bumper, boot lid and both tail lamps damaged. Police report filed at the scene.
cases.why: Collision is own damage by accidental external means (Motor 3.1); no exclusion applies.

cases.title: Motor theft, keys left in the ignition
cases.description: Car stolen from outside my house in the evening. I had left the keys in the ignition while I carried shopping bags inside for a few minutes. FIR filed the same night.
cases.why: Theft with the keys in the vehicle is excluded (Motor 4.4).

cases.title: Motor flood, engine cranked in water
cases.description: Drove into a waterlogged underpass during heavy rain and the engine stalled in the water. I tried to restart it twice. The garage says water was drawn into the cylinders and the engine needs an overhaul; there is no other damage.
cases.why: Engine damage from water drawn in after cranking (hydrostatic lock) is excluded without the Engine Protection add-on (Motor 4.3). Escalating is acceptable because the schedule's add-ons are not in the data.

cases.title: Motor collision while over the alcohol limit
cases.description: Hit the road divider at night on the way back from a party. The police breath test at the scene showed alcohol above the legal limit. Front bumper, bonnet and radiator damaged.
cases.why: Driving under the influence of alcohol beyond the legal limit is a general exclusion (Motor 4.1).

cases.title: Motor theft, no detail on keys or locks
cases.description: Vehicle stolen from outside residence overnight; FIR filed.
cases.why: Theft is covered (Motor 3.1). Whether the car was locked is unknown, which is a question for the reviewer, not a reason to reject. This is the claim that used to burn both reflection retries.

cases.title: Health, wrist fracture from a fall
cases.description: Fell from a ladder while cleaning the ceiling fan at home and fractured my right wrist. Admitted for three days for surgery to fix the fracture.
cases.why: Accidental injury is covered from day one and no waiting period applies (Health 3.6).

cases.title: Health, cataract inside the 24-month waiting period
cases.description: Cataract surgery on the left eye, performed as a day care procedure.
cases.why: Cataract is covered only after 24 months of continuous coverage (Health 5.2), and this is the customer's first policy.

cases.title: Health, cosmetic surgery
cases.description: Elective liposuction and abdominoplasty for weight reduction. No accident, burns or cancer involved.
cases.why: Cosmetic surgery and treatment for weight control are excluded (Health 6.1).

cases.title: Health, dengue admission
cases.description: Admitted for four days with dengue fever; platelet count dropped and needed monitoring and IV fluids.
cases.why: Medically necessary inpatient hospitalisation is covered (Health 3.1); the 30-day initial waiting period has passed.

cases.title: Home, burst pipe
cases.description: A pipe burst suddenly in the upstairs bathroom overnight. Water came through the ceiling and damaged the living room ceiling and the wooden flooring.
cases.why: Sudden and accidental bursting of a pipe is covered (Home 3.3).

cases.title: Home, slow roof leak
cases.description: Over the last few months damp patches have spread across the bedroom wall and the paint is peeling. A plumber found a slow leak where the roof meets the wall.
cases.why: Damage from water leaking or seeping over time, including damp patches and leaks through roofs, is excluded (Home 6.2).

cases.title: Home, jewellery missing with no forced entry
cases.description: Came back from a two-week trip and found gold jewellery missing from a bedroom drawer. All doors and windows were locked and there are no signs of forced entry.
cases.why: Theft without evidence of forcible entry is excluded (Home 6.4); burglary cover requires forcible entry (Home 3.4).

cases.title: Rule R01, amount above the sum insured
cases.description: Windscreen smashed and side panels scratched while parked.
cases.why: Claiming 650,000 on a 500,000 sum insured scores 70 and exceeds the auto-decision limit: a person must cap the payout.

cases.title: Rule R02, policy lapsed before the incident
cases.description: Planned knee arthroscopy.
cases.why: The policy lapsed for a missed premium before the incident: a hard block. Arthroscopy would also still be in its 24-month waiting period.

cases.title: Rule R03, claim 12 days after the policy started
cases.description: Roof and bonnet dented by a falling tree during a cyclone while parked.
cases.why: A new-policy claim scores 40, below the escalation threshold, and cyclone damage is covered (Motor 3.1). Section 5.2 asks for verification, not an exclusion, so escalating is also defensible.

cases.title: Rule R04, fourth claim in a year
cases.description: Burst pipe in the upstairs bathroom damaged ceilings and flooring.
cases.why: Frequent claims score 35, below the escalation threshold, and a burst pipe is covered (Home 3.3).

cases.title: Rule R05, incident date in the future
cases.description: Vehicle stolen from outside residence overnight; FIR filed.
cases.why: An incident dated after submission is a hard block.

cases.title: Rule R06, incident before the policy started
cases.description: Admitted for four days with dengue fever.
cases.why: The incident happened 15 days before cover began: a hard block.

cases.title: Rule R07, duplicate of an approved claim
cases.description: Rear-ended at a traffic signal; bumper and tail lamp damaged.
cases.why: Same policy, date and amount as an approved claim scores 70: paying the same loss twice must be ruled out by a person.

cases.title: Rule R08, KYC pending
cases.description: Cataract procedure performed as day care.
cases.why: Pending KYC scores 70: no payment may be released until identity is verified (anti-money-laundering).
